properties.name: The allocation layer is corrected against the artifact layer
properties.rationale:
THE HEADLINE WAS WRONG AND THE ARTIFACT LAYER ALREADY KNEW. `unallocated_component` reported "33 of 85 parts hold no function"; 31 of the 33 are real source modules with a linked, checksummed file, and for most of them the module header cites by id the very capability the design had filed elsewhere — coverage.rs names cap:coverage (allocated to cmp:drift), regions.rs names cap:a-session-with-no-seed-can-find-one (allocated to cmp:scope).

The lesson is about the CHECK, not only the design: a detector that reads one layer and reports absence, while a second layer in the same graph holds the answer, states something stronger than it measured. That is the failure `dec:reflow2-is-built-for-observability` exists to forbid — an answer that misrepresents what the design knows. The cross-layer comparison this event records was done by hand in a Python script over the export; nothing in reflow2 offers it.

Recorded as `subject: record` deliberately: not one line of the system changed. Only the design's account of where its own functions live.
properties.subject: record
properties.summary: Measured every allocated Capability against the file that REALIZES it: 59 agree, 23 disagree, 130 carry no file evidence either way. 19 of the 23 disagreements name an implementing module that the design was reporting as holding NO function — the function was captured, and filed against a neighbouring module. Corrects those allocations to the module whose code implements them, on Anthony's word 2026-08-25 (move it, do not dual-allocate).
